The decision is **CONTINUE**. Round 337 is **SYS-R336-PERF-DRAG-WINDOW**, a test-only cleanup of the interactions perf harness on baseline `f1def9c`. On my sketch every perf row value stayed the same.

**Round 336 closed.** C passed RETRO 336: 10 rows, 0 bugs, browser-verified at both viewports. Gate 336 was skipped because nothing in `store/` changed, so the baseline stays gate 335's `f1def9c`. The round-336 task is archived as `tasks/round-336.md`, a byte-equal copy. C left four notes, all recorded:
- **Wrong expected label (my task text):** the smoke row expected "Undo: Move clip" for a cross-lane drag, but the app correctly says "Move to track — Stems". Not an app bug.
- **Script overwrite:** one of my analysis scripts writes into its own folder, and C's re-run overwrote a file there (C restored it). I logged it as a lesson candidate.
- **Status wording:** a backlog status read slightly differently from the task text. Closed as info.
- **Saba's questions:** C reproduced the two screen-review candidates SR-336-1/2; they stay with Saba.

**Why this task now.** Today is 2026-11-04, before the 2026-11-05 regression date. Under the rule fixed last round, that makes 337 SYS-R336. The regression round comes at the first planning on or after 2026-11-05.

**What round 337 changes.** A owns four files:
- **`perf/studio-lab-interactions.perf.spec.ts`:**
  - shared helpers replace the duplicated code in the two drag functions: `dragWindow`, `rowWriter`, `componentsPerMove` and `pressedGesture`;
  - `pressedGesture` releases the mouse button if a gesture fails;
  - named constants `laneSegmentSteps`/`laneSegmentPx` replace `dragSteps / 6` and `dragDistancePx / 3`;
  - the pass-order text now matches the code (Ctrl+wheel runs after the final Space).
- **`perf/budgets.interactions.json`:** only the `note` field of 58 rows changes. The repeated gesture sentence is shortened, and the denominator wording is corrected in the older drag notes too, which had the same error.
- **Doc 233:** a new implementation doc.
- **Doc 168:** the `## მეტრიკები` section only.

**One premise did not hold, so I changed the acceptance.** The gate reviewer said a failed read leaves the button down and the next step starts mid-gesture. At HEAD that can't happen: a throw aborts the whole pass and closes its browser context. The release fix stays as hygiene. It is now tested by something the harness can actually observe: whether the page records a pointer release after the injected failure.

**What I ran on my sketch** (a scratch copy outside `store/`, which stayed clean throughout):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Perf spec alone, production build, v1 and v2 | 139 of 139 non-wallclock rows equal to C's round-335 run, 0 different, 0 new; row ids identical (193); 36/36 asserted rows pass; every liveness row 1 |
| Notes check | 58 notes changed, no other field changed |
| perf/lib report test | 34/34 |
| typecheck | passes |
| Mutant P (release kept, injected failure) | release recorded: `true` |
| Mutant M (release removed) | release recorded: `false` |
| Mutant D (per-move formula changed) | red on exactly the 9 predicted rows, 73 rows unchanged |

The 1-pass mutant runs exit with code 1 by design, because the 6× rows aren't measured. The task says so, so A won't treat that as a failure.

**Sketch review.** `code-reviewer` isn't on this phase's consult list, so I used `tech-lead` and recorded the substitution. It found nothing at Medium or above. I applied three of its five Lows in v2, and the v2 perf run is the evidence. A still runs the real code-reviewer on its own tree.

**Advisor.** It was available and consulted twice: before writing and before finishing. After the second call I made the commands in the task state their working directory, added a recipe for A's mutant copies, and replaced a mutant example for C that could never change a value. I also added a stale-text sweep, which found 0 hits.

**Written:** `current-task.md`, `backlog.json` v296, `feature-status.md`, `b-round-336.md` and `b-next.json` (CONTINUE, 36 remaining items). The claims script and all evidence are in `b-round-336/`, and the claims were re-run after the last edit. Still waiting on root: architecture checkpoint D-29z915 and the perf-test config request.
